page: Amazon Web Services d3en.6xlarge is a dense storage instance optimized for network and EBS throughput. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with 24 vCPUs (12 physical cores) operating at 3.1 GHz, supported by 96.0 GB of DDR4 memory. The system is built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes a massive 167,760 GB of local HDD storage, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile. Single-core CPU performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% with a Geekbench single-core score of 1056.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1327.3. However, multi-core operations perform at an average level, as demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 8267.0 and a passmark CPU score of 20039.62. Memory bandwidth also remains in the middle 50% tier, reaching 108.25 GB/sec for large block read-only operations.

The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance lies in its high storage density, offering a massive volume of local HDD capacity relative to its compute resources. This makes it suitable for workloads requiring high sequential disk throughput and large storage footprints rather than high random IOPS or intensive single-threaded compute. Appropriate workloads include distributed file systems, data lakes, large-scale log analysis, and backup repositories.
